title: Dairy and food microbiology
tables: Dairies, food processors, ingredient manufacturers and food-testing labs.
High-volume plate counts and spoilage/indicator assays create repetitive work and release delays.
Plate handling; RGB imaging; colony counting; incubation; barcode/PIMS; LIMS; optional inhibition-zone assay.
Map batch/sample -> run approved culture or inhibition method -> automated image/count/measurement -> QC and exception review -> release/hold data to LIMS.
Counts, growth kinetics, inhibition measurements where applicable, images, batch linkage and reviewer disposition.
Improves throughput, consistency and cross-shift traceability for plate-based methods.
Antibiotic-residue detection requires a validated assay and controls; AMR-Eye cannot infer residue identity from a plate image alone. Food matrices and methods require separate validation.
